sources.locator: Introduction and Figure 1: Atlantic flow splits between Scandinavia and Svalbard into Barents inflow via Bear Island Trough and northward WSC continuation; shelf/slope components differ.
sources.supports: Regional northward continuation after Barents inflow split; selected departure coordinates are not source endpoints.

sources.citation: Menze et al. (2019), Atlantic Water Pathways Along the North-Western Svalbard Shelf Mapped Using Vessel-Mounted Current Profilers, JGR Oceans, doi:10.1029/2018JC014299.
sources.locator: Abstract; sections 4.3 and 6: northward boundary flow at 79-80 N / 5-10 E, splitting into Svalbard, Yermak and Yermak Pass branches.
sources.role: Northern branch-region context; summer composite does not establish all branches at every time.

sources.citation: Dundas and Fer (2026), Atlantic Water flow through Fram Strait to the Arctic Ocean measured by repeated glider transects, Ocean Science 22, 1003-1021.
sources.locator: Introduction; sections 2.1-2.2 and code/data availability: separate slope/front branches, 77.25 N target section and limited season coverage.
sources.role: Source-specific naming and section/season caveats; transect distances are not current length or width.

route_convention.vertices: All OSW selected; no axis or isobath digitized.
route_convention.excluded_paths: Offshore front feeder, Barents inflow, recirculation, shelf/fjord intrusions, downstream named branches.

related_ledger_name.name: Spitsbergen Atlantic Current
related_ledger_name.scope: NOAA describes a northwestward flow off southwest Spitsbergen; alias or component relationship to WSC not established.

seasonal_evidence.composite_guard: Not all branches present at every sampled time.
seasonal_evidence.season_definition: Source uses 15 November to distinguish autumn/winter sections; not universal calendar seasons.

section_guards: Glider target at 77.25 N is a transect, not an along-current path.
342 km full transect and 200/300 km region divisions are analysis support, not WSC width.
Absolute geostrophic reconstruction uses altimetry as reference after erroneous depth-average-current estimates; uncorrected DAC must not be reused.
Transport and transport uncertainty cannot supply length/width ranges.

data_access_leads.role: Summer ADCP data cited by Menze; records, reuse and geographic coverage not acquired/validated.
Glider archive cited by Dundas/Fer; records, reuse and seasonal coverage not acquired/validated.
